low back pain.source: WHO Package of Interventions for Rehabilitation (PIR)
interventions: Manual therapy (spinal manipulation and mobilization) as an adjunct.
Education on self-management, remaining active, and pain neuroscience.
Psychological therapies (CBT) for chronic pain with psychosocial risk factors.
assistive_products: Lumbar supports (rarely recommended for acute pain)

stroke.source: WHO Package of Interventions for Rehabilitation (PIR)
interventions: Task-specific repetitive training for upper and lower limb recovery.
Gait training including treadmill and overground walking.
Speech and language therapy for aphasia.
Spasticity management (positioning, orthoses, botulinum toxin adjunct).
